feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear progression, credible scope, and relevant technical depth. It reads polished and substantive, but impact would improve with tighter formatting, fewer repeated themes, and more outcome-focused metrics in several roles.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director; this strengthens credibility and leadership narrative.  
- Strong blend of strategy and execution: digital leadership, CMS/platform work, analytics, multimedia, and governance are all well represented.  
- Writing is generally polished and professional, with no obvious misspellings; examples like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools add specificity.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Summary, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT. The same ideas appear multiple times, which weakens structure and scannability.  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope/activity, especially in freelance and earlier roles: growth %, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, revenue/member impact, or campaign results.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); and keep punctuation/bullet formatting consistent across sections.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads a bit generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of scale and a tighter focus on recent leadership-level work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Add clearer seniority and scope, e.g., “leading digital strategy and cross-channel communications for mission-driven and membership organizations.”
- Replace broad phrases like “expert in” with sharper, evidence-backed language tied to recent work: web modernization, editorial systems, analytics, and advocacy communications.
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social media, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, Drupal-based web modernization, editorial workflow design, and analytics-driven communications operations. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear content, aligning stakeholders, and building systems that support large, complex teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “advocacy messaging” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Avoid overloading the intro with platform/tool language already covered in skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of strategic, technical, and communications capabilities, but several items are broad or overlap heavily with the summary and Topline Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership themes will make this section sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with more senior, specific language: “Multi-channel communications leadership,” “Web platform governance,” and “Editorial systems & workflow design.”
- Reduce overlap by combining similar items: merge “Workflow & systems architecture” with “Editorial workflow design,” and simplify “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination.”
- Align style and parallel structure; use either all nouns or all noun phrases.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS administration • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital strategy & transformation” and “Policy & advocacy communication(s)” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- This section overlaps significantly with Topline Skills; keep Core Competencies broader and let Topline Skills carry the tool/platform detail.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Make it sharper by foregrounding scope, platform leadership, and any measurable outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter summary line: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed and implemented digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices that improved coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Consolidate Drupal/CMS bullets: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, modular storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits; provided front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, publishing time reduced, search success uplift, or engagement gains from the AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this bullet shorter here.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also echo the header and NACo role—avoid repeating broad capability language.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It would be stronger if the opening were tighter, bullets started with clearer outcomes, and channel-management points were less repetitive with earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel bullet and add measurable results if available: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials; improved engagement/reporting through centralized channel strategy.”
- Make ops/analytics bullets more impact-driven: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to strengthen executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version at a higher strategic/organizational level.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed here as building enterprise capability (studio, scale, in-house production).

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and any concrete growth or process outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member-facing communications.”
- Combine and sharpen bullets around owned outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show build-out and impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add measurable workflow/editorial outcomes if available: e.g., publishing volume, turnaround time, campaign cadence, stakeholder groups supported, or engagement growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved workflows” and “strengthened editorial planning” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language; keep this version focused on hands-on execution.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; clarify this role as scaling/formalizing the series, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

- Suggested rewrite:

- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than exhaustive technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-signal or dated items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is essential for target roles.
- Put the most relevant/recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization and migration” instead of just “CMS modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let the Technical section hold the full tool inventory.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in the header/core competencies, so avoid overemphasizing it here unless it is a target-role differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than just platform names.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI and Looker Studio” + “KPI framework design” + “executive/leadership reporting” + “SEO and digital performance analysis.”
- Consider adding one higher-value phrase such as “measurement architecture” or “analytics infrastructure” to better match recent Director-level work.
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics infrastructure • Measurement strategy & KPI design • Executive reporting dashboards • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio & Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.
- Tool list also overlaps with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep this section more strategic, and leave full tool inventory there.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera and studio systems,” “Virtual event production workflows.”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent CMS experience or expanded with level/context.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, order by strength/relevance: put **Drupal** first and consider adding proficiency cues like **Advanced** for Drupal if used elsewhere consistently.
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it was only lightly used; replace with a more meaningful qualifier on Drupal or SharePoint.
- Keep this item platform-only; save implementation details for the coding/technical line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or making this one more concise.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating generic CMS terms without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery; **Integrations & deployment:** API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions; **Tagging & tracking:** Google Tag Manager
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use version-specific naming; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- Consider replacing broad terms with stronger phrasing if accurate: “REST API integrations,” “serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers),” “CI/CD automation (GitHub Actions).”
- If possible, connect to outcomes elsewhere in the CV by adding examples in experience bullets rather than here, e.g., tagging, deployment automation, or custom front-end work that improved launch speed or tracking quality.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may also overlap with GitHub Actions unless differentiated.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function to improve scanability: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/Workflow Management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses for stronger positioning, e.g. **Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana (cross-team planning)**
- Consider trimming lower-value/general tools if space is tight; keep the platforms most tied to recent systems/governance work

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; they add less differentiation than Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, or Asana

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale or use case. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, keep this as a concise platform list rather than repeating newsletter achievements.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and ATS: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add functional context instead of outcomes: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Example rewrite: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Campaign automation • Newsletter distribution • Audience segmentation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already covered in recent work experience.
- Don’t repeat broad “multi-channel communications” language already captured in Core Competencies and role descriptions.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete scope or outputs if you can add them.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten and specify contributions: “Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations; helped streamline publishing workflows and cross-channel content production.”
- Add measurable outputs where possible: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, or team size.
- Suggested rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations, improved publishing workflows, contributed to a major website refresh, and produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates. Provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this role as launching/producing the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating governance/operations language already used more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the distinctive innovation/research scope and tighten the media language.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the broader function, then the standout result: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities…”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with clearer ownership: “produced digital and multimedia content” or “supported development of digital and multimedia materials.”
- Tighten the podcast clause to show initiative and end-to-end execution: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- If available, add one concrete outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or how research informed program/policy work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item focused on innovation/research + first podcast.
- Avoid broad claims about digital leadership here, since stronger, more recent evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.
